sources.entry: Beyond the Prompt: Claude Code by Arpan Patel - This has what you need. Remarkably clear, information-dense, it's Claude Code: the good parts, for beginners, advanced users, pets, anybody.

summary.name: Beyond the Prompt: Claude Code
summary.one_liner: A long practical guide to getting more out of Claude Code, covering the .claude directory, CLAUDE.md files, skills, subagents, plugins, slash commands, MCP servers, and daily workflow patterns.
use_cases: Setting up project and global Claude Code configuration
Writing a concise CLAUDE.md that prevents repeat mistakes
Building reusable slash-command skills for a team
Delegating code review or codebase research to subagents
Running large migrations across parallel worktree agents
Connecting Claude Code to GitHub, Sentry, Linear or Obsidian via MCP
summary.what_it_does: The guide is a tutorial-style page written by a daily Claude Code user, presenting workflow patterns such as using plan mode before multi-file changes, referencing exact files, and letting Claude write its own rules into CLAUDE.md after mistakes. It explains the layered .claude configuration (CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, settings files, skills, commands, agents, rules) with a scope table. It documents how to write skills and custom subagents with frontmatter, gives example Go and PR-review definitions, and lists popular community and official skills, subagents, and plugins. It also covers underused slash commands such as /compact, /rewind, /batch, /loop and /goal, and how to connect MCP servers.
notable: Explains the .claude directory scopes and a file-by-file table of what to commit versus keep local
Covers CLAUDE.md writing philosophy attributed to Boris Cherny, including a real team CLAUDE.md example
Includes full example SKILL.md and subagent files, plus an Obsidian MCP workflow with a three-tier memory layout
Documents newer commands such as /goal, /insights, /batch and /rewind
caveats: Plugin count and some details are described as of mid-2026 and may change
Several workflow claims are the author's personal experience rather than verified benchmarks
The page does not state pricing for Claude Code itself
